newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends stronger in muted response to RBNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends stronger in muted response to RBNZ.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended stronger on Monday in a largely muted response to the latest missive from the Reserve Bank, but dealers were not ruling out a push higher as the week progressed.
Early in the afternoon session the Reserve Bank said monetary conditions had been become too loose and warned that it would take steps, if necessary, to rectify matters.
The Kiwi then rallied about 20 basis points from its 0.6413/20 open but struck stiff resistance at 0.6440, with offshore sellers emerging at that level.
By the close the currency was at 0.6434/39. The Trade-Weighted Index also firmer at 64.16 from 64.06.
"I think that it is due for a move higher," said one Auckland dealer.
Once the selling interest had been satisfied at around 0.6440 level there was a good chance the currency could hit 0.6500 over the next week, he added.
Dealers doubted today's move would be convincing enough for the Reserve Bank.
Another dealer expected the bank to re-enter the fray if the the currency does not move substantially higher from here.
"I think it (today's statement) was regarded as a toothless comment and the price action reflected that," he said.
"We are still very dependent on different asset markets so I think that still holds the key to the equation," he said.
Today's move by the RBNZ was looked like it was designed to buy time before the central bank's next statement on September 18, he said.
